question: A 65-year-old female patient developed speech apraxia two years earlier and has evolved a rigid-akinetic parkinsonism predominantly in the right half of the body with superimposed myoclonus and foreign hand phenomenon or foreign limb. Which diagnosis do you consider most likely?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Speech apraxia -> Rigid-akinetic parkinsonism predominantly in the right half of the body -> Myoclonus and foreign limb phenomenon -> Corticobasal degeneration -> opb. Corticobasal degeneration -> 80%
CHAIN: Speech apraxia -> Rigid-akinetic parkinsonism predominantly in the right half of the body -> Myoclonus and foreign limb phenomenon -> Parkinson's disease -> opa. Parkinson's disease -> 70%
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of speech apraxia, rigid-akinetic parkinsonism predominantly in the right half of the body, myoclonus, and foreign limb phenomenon, the most likely diagnosis is corticobasal degeneration.
